title: Portrait and Will
premise: When Rafael Fairweather, the reclusive coroner of Hollowmere, is ordered to exhume town founder Edmund Voss for a land dispute, they find the coffin empty and a fresh portrait of Rafael tucked inside. The killer, it emerges, is Rafael's old mentor and former coroner, Ida Marsh, who faked Voss's death decades ago to cover up his murder of her sister — and who has spent years watching Rafael to ensure the secret stayed buried. As bodies begin surfacing in the pattern of an old case file only two people ever read, Rafael must choose between protecting the mentor who saved their life and exposing a truth that will unravel the town itself. In the end, Rafael traps Ida with a forged exhumation report, but chooses to reveal everything anyway, paying the price of survival by finally becoming visible.
about_author: Xanthe Yarrow is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent years cataloguing death certificates in county archives before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about small towns where everyone knows the dead better than the living.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Rafael Fairweather's POV. Establishes Hollowmere and Rafael's quiet, invisible life among its graves as a court order forces the exhumation of founder Edmund Voss. Emotional beat: uneasy routine disrupted — Rafael dreads the disturbance of a grave they've tended for thirty years.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The coffin opens on nothing but soil and a small oil portrait of Rafael themselves, painted recently. The sheriff dismisses it as a prank; Rafael recognizes the brushwork style from somewhere they can't place. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into personal violation.

chapters.title: What the File Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with flashbacks. Digging into archived records, Rafael finds gaps in the 1971 case files — pages cut cleanly out — and realizes whoever did this knew the archive intimately. Emotional beat: the past pressing against the present like a hand on the shoulder.

chapters.title: A Visit from Ida
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Retired coroner Ida Marsh, Rafael's mentor, arrives unannounced, offering help while asking oddly precise questions about the investigation. Warmth laced with wrongness. Emotional beat: comfort curdling into suspicion Rafael refuses to feel yet.

chapters.title: Second Grave, Same Hand
chapters.summary: Deputy Cora Lin's POV (new investigator). A body surfaces matching details from the missing 1971 file pages — details never made public. Cora suspects an insider; Rafael realizes the killer is replaying the old case. Emotional beat: mounting terror of being hunted by someone fluent in your own methods.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Researching Voss's family, Rafael finds a daughter erased from every record: Lila Marsh — Ida's sister, who died the same week Voss 'died.' Emotional beat: grief and betrayal colliding as the portrait's painter becomes obvious.

chapters.title: Confession at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida confronts Rafael privately, admitting she helped cover Voss's murder of Lila because no one would believe a servant girl over the town's founder — and because exposing it would have destroyed young Rafael too. She asks for loyalty one last time. Emotional beat: love against duty, laid bare.

chapters.title: The Third Portrait
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. A third body appears with another portrait — this time of Cora — proving Ida is eliminating everyone closing in. Rafael, suspected of complicity, is suspended. Emotional beat: isolation; the trap closing from all sides, with time running out.

chapters.title: Exhumation, Reversed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael plants a forged report claiming Voss's remains were found hidden beneath the courthouse, baiting Ida into destroying the evidence herself. The climax unfolds in the crypt: Ida confesses fully, knife drawn, and Rafael talks her down just as Cora arrives. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth decided in a single breath.

chapters.title: Portrait and Will
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ida, dying of illness she'd hidden, leaves Rafael a will containing Lila's true testimony and a final self-portrait. Rafael publishes everything — the murder, the cover-up, their own silence — accepting exile from the town's good graces. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid willingly; visibility chosen at last.
